Introduction
What is climate?
The typical weather expected, based on data from many years
The present state of the atmosphere at a given time
The amount of rain that falls in one day
The wind speed and direction at a given place
Climate is determined by weather reports over a long period: the typical weather expected for an area.
Introduction
What does 'weather' refer to?
The present state of the atmosphere and current conditions
The average conditions over many years
The rainfall expected in a typical year
The height at which clouds form
Weather refers to the present state of the atmosphere and describes current conditions.
Introduction
Which saying sums up the difference between climate and weather?
Climate is what you expect and weather is what you get
Weather is what you expect and climate is what you get
Climate changes daily but weather never changes
Weather is measured but climate is only guessed
The manual uses the saying: 'Climate is what you expect and weather is what you get.'
Measuring weather
Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
A barometer
An anemometer
A rain gauge
A thermometer
Barometers are instruments used in meteorology to measure atmospheric pressure.
Measuring weather
Which instrument is used to measure wind speed?
An anemometer
A barometer
A thermometer
A rain gauge
Anemometers are used for measuring wind speed and wind pressure.
Measuring weather
What is the ideal height for an anemometer?
10 m in open terrain
1 m in open terrain
10 m next to a building
100 m on a hilltop
The ideal height for anemometers is 10 m in open terrain, as trees, valleys and buildings affect readings.
Measuring weather
Where should a thermometer be kept?
In the shade, away from precipitation and direct sunlight
In direct sunlight, away from any shade
Inside a closed vehicle
Buried just under the surface of the soil
Thermometers are kept in the shade, away from any form of precipitation or direct sunlight.
Measuring weather
Where should a rain gauge be set up?
In open ground away from objects that may affect it
Under a large tree to protect it
Next to a building for shelter
On the roof of a vehicle
The gauge is set in open ground away from any object which may influence the measurements.
Factors influencing our weather
Which ocean current is cold and moves north along the Namibian coast?
The Benguela current
The Agulhas current
The Mozambique current
The Equatorial current
The Benguela current off the west coast is a cold current from the Antarctic moving north along the Namibian shoreline.
Factors influencing our weather
Why do onshore winds from the Benguela current bring little rain?
The cold water gives off little moisture
The winds blow too fast to form clouds
The Drakensberg blocks the winds
The water is too warm to form clouds
Because the water is cold, onshore winds collect limited moisture, which is deposited as mist a few kilometres inland.
Factors influencing our weather
Where does the warm Agulhas current come from?
The equator
The Antarctic
The Atlantic Ocean
The Arctic
The Agulhas current comes from the equator, bringing warm water along the Mozambique/KwaZulu-Natal coast.
Factors influencing our weather
Why is Botswana's rainfall lower than that of its eastern neighbours?
Most rain from the east falls before the clouds reach Botswana
The Benguela current brings dry air from the east
Botswana is too high for clouds to form
Cold fronts from the south block all rain
Most of the rain falls over the eastern belt; by the time clouds reach Botswana there is little water vapour left.
Factors influencing our weather
What does the Inter-tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) bring to Botswana in summer?
Widespread rain for days at a time
Cold, dry winds from the south
Thick mist a few kilometres inland
Hot, dry weather with no clouds
Warm, moist air from the north is undercut by cold fronts from the south, causing widespread rain for days at a time.
Factors influencing our weather
In winter, what prevents clouds and rain forming over the interior?
A strong high pressure system
A low pressure system
Warm, moist air from the Indian Ocean
The Inter-tropical Convergence Zone
The winter diagram shows a strong high pressure system dominating the interior, preventing clouds and rain.
Temperatures and rainfall
In which month do temperatures in Botswana peak?
October
December
January
July
Temperatures peak in October when there is little or no cloud cover and minor wind movement.
Temperatures and rainfall
Which is Botswana's coldest month?
July
May
June
August
Botswana's coldest month is July, when it may drop to below freezing point.
Temperatures and rainfall
According to the table, which town has the highest average rainfall?
Kasane (650 mm)
Gaborone (530 mm)
Maun (460 mm)
Ghanzi (430 mm)
The table shows Kasane with 650 mm, the highest of the towns listed.
Clouds
What is evaporation?
Water changing from a liquid to a gas
A gas or vapour changing to a liquid
Water changing from a liquid to ice
Ice changing straight into rain
Evaporation is the process of water changing from a liquid to a gaseous form.
Clouds
What is condensation?
A gas or vapour changing to a liquid
A liquid changing to a gas
Air rising and becoming warmer
Rain soaking into the ground
Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour to a liquid, by cooling or by increased pressure.
Clouds
According to the manual, what is the height at which clouds form called?
The dew point
The inversion layer
The occluded front
The watershed
The manual states that the height at which clouds form in the atmosphere is known as dew point.
Clouds
How does an occluded front form?
A warm air mass is caught between two cold fronts and forced up
Two warm air masses meet over the ocean
Cold air is trapped below an inversion layer
Warm air sinks on the leeward side of a mountain
An occluded front forms when a warm air mass is caught between two cold fronts and the whole warm mass is forced to rise.
Clouds
Which clouds are high clouds that usually contain ice crystals?
Cirrus clouds
Stratus clouds
Alto clouds
Nimbus clouds
Cirrus are high clouds (6 000 to 12 000 m) that usually contain ice crystals.
Clouds
At what height range are 'alto' (midrange) clouds found?
The cloud table gives the alto level as 2 000 to 6 000 m.
Clouds
What does the Latin word 'cumulus' mean?
Heap or pile
Sheet
Rain
Curling lock of hair
Cumulus means heap or pile; stratus means sheet, cirrus a curling lock of hair and nimbus rain.
Clouds
What does the Latin word 'nimbus' mean?
Rain
Heap or pile
Sheet
Curling lock of hair
The manual states that nimbus means rain.
Clouds
Which cloud type is classed as multi-level?
Cumulonimbus
Cirrostratus
Stratocumulus
Altocumulus
Of the 10 prominent cloud types, cumulonimbus is the multi-level cloud.
Lightning
What is lightning?
A large electrostatic discharge from unbalanced electric charges
Sunlight reflecting off ice crystals in clouds
Super-heated rain falling from a cloud
Burning dust particles in the atmosphere
Lightning is a large electrostatic discharge caused by an imbalance in the electric charges in the atmosphere.
Lightning
Which clouds usually produce lightning?
Cumulonimbus clouds
Cirrus clouds
Altostratus clouds
Stratus clouds
Lightning is usually associated with and produced by cumulonimbus clouds.
Lightning
What causes thunder?
Rapid expansion and contraction of air super-heated by lightning
Clouds bumping into each other
Hail hitting the ground at high speed
Ice crystals breaking inside the cloud
Thunder results from the rapid expansion and contraction of air molecules super-heated by the lightning.
Lightning
How does lightning benefit plant life?
It leads to the formation of nitric acid in the air
It kills insects that eat the plants
It burns old grass to make ash
It warms the soil so seeds can germinate
Lightning ionises the air, forming nitric oxide and ultimately nitric acid, which benefits the plant life below.
Rainfall
Where does relief rainfall occur in southern Africa?
Along the east coast, against the Drakensberg
Along the west coast of Namibia
Over the centre of the Kalahari
Over the Okavango Delta
Relief rainfall occurs along the east coast where moist air is forced up against the Drakensberg mountain range.
Rainfall
What happens to clouds as they pass onto the leeward side of a mountain?
The air sinks and warms, so the droplets turn back into vapour
The air rises and cools, so more rain falls
The clouds freeze and fall as hail
The clouds stay the same and keep moving
On the leeward side the air sinks and the temperature increases, so the droplets become water vapour once more.
Rainfall
How does convection rain begin?
The sun heats the Earth's surface, warming the air above it
Moist air is forced up against a mountain range
A cold current cools the air along the coast
A warm air mass is trapped between two cold fronts
Convection rain begins with the sun heating the Earth's surface; the warm air rises, cools and condenses.
Safety precautions
When does hyperthermia occur?
When the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can lose
When the body loses more heat than it produces
When a person drinks too much water
When a person is out in cold winds and hail
Hyperthermia occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate; it is a medical emergency.
Safety precautions
What are the most common causes of hyperthermia?
Heat stroke and adverse reactions to some medications
Cold winds and hailstorms
Drinking alcohol and smoking
Lightning strikes and flash floods
The most common causes of hyperthermia are heat stroke and adverse reactions to certain medications.
Safety precautions
During a storm, where can you often find adequate shelter?
On the leeward side of a hill
Under a large tree
In an aluminium boat
On top of a hill
The leeward side of a hill often provides adequate protection until the storm has abated.
Safety precautions
Why should guides not shelter in aluminium boats during a lightning storm?
Aluminium boats conduct lightning
Aluminium boats sink in heavy rain
Aluminium boats are blown over by wind
Aluminium boats get too hot
The manual warns that aluminium boats will conduct lightning, so guides should find shelter on land.
Safety precautions
What should a guide do if out in mokoros when a storm approaches?
Pole to shore as soon as possible
Stay in the open water until it passes
Shelter under the nearest tree
Tie the mokoros together and wait
Avoid being out in the open; if in mokoros, pole to shore as soon as possible.
Safety precautions
Which is a typical symptom of hypothermia?
Shivering
Heavy sweating
Very red, hot skin
Extreme thirst
Typical symptoms of hypothermia are shivering, lethargy, confusion, apathy, delirium and heart rhythm irregularities.
Safety precautions
Why should alcohol never be used to treat hypothermia?
It reduces the core body temperature
It raises the core body temperature too fast
It makes the person shiver more
It causes heat stroke
Alcohol may give a feeling of warmth, but it reduces core body temperature, making hypothermia worse.
Safety precautions
What should be carried on longer activities in case of hypothermia?
Space blankets
Extra fuel
Alcohol
Ice packs
Protective clothing should be provided and space blankets carried as a precautionary measure.
